thumbnail.analysis: Registered maxresdefault 1280x720 (HTTP 200, real image). White field. Left: the recurring cartoon man, hands on cheeks, screaming. Right: black headline "THEY TAKE EVERYTHING"; below, grey clawed hands rising from the ground clutching a house, a pickup truck and a cash stack, with a black arrow from the man. At 320x180 the headline and the house/truck read clearly. The thumbnail promises the opposite of the script's thesis (most bills cannot take anything quickly), a fear hook the video then defuses.

script.opening_words: There's a stack of envelopes on your kitchen counter. You know what's inside, which is why you haven't opened them in weeks. A hospital bill, a past-due notice, the amount in red, one of those windowed envelopes that's never good news, and somewhere in your brain, a voice has already written the ending. A repo truck idling at 6:00 a.m., a sheriff at your door, maybe a jail cell with your name on it. So, you keep juggling money you
script.ending_words: wakes up something that was already dead. So, tonight, do the one thing the little voice has been begging you not to do. Open the envelopes, sort them into their buckets, and handle them in the order that protects your life, not the order that yells the loudest. The monster under the bed was never a monster. It was a calendar the whole time. And now, you can read it.
script.analysis: Full 19232 canonical characters read. A single-narrator debt-consequence explainer: hook (unopened envelopes), three debt buckets, credit cards day by day with Clark ($6,000), medical debt, car repossession and deficiency, utilities and cold-weather rules, rent and court eviction, federal student-loan default and garnishment, the IRS (penalties, passport), collector rules and statutes of limitations, private garnishment limits, credit-score damage, and a payment-priority order. Mostly accurate; the student-loan garnishment narrative omits the January 2026 pause.
beat_map: Hook: unopened bills and worst-case fears.
Credit cards: late fees, 30-day reporting, Clark, charge-off, debt buyers.
Debt collectors, statutes of limitations, zombie debt.
